headline: Medium risk overall: RD-Agent’s browser/API automation can leak or cascade errors, while LightZero is read-only and non-networked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem, browser, MCP, or network surfaces, so it cannot ingest RD-Agent output by default. RD-Agent can browse and call APIs, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel; only unusual manual copy-paste or external orchestration would bridge them. That makes prompt injection possible but not default and with limited blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies RD-Agent output into a LightZero prompt or file
IF an external orchestrator adds a shared clipboard, queue, or filesystem bridge
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate terminals with no shared clipboard
Disable copy-paste of model outputs into LightZero prompts
Use a human review step before any text from RD-Agent reaches LightZero
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches logs, execution traces, competition datasets, and secrets, and it sends data to third-party APIs by default. LightZero is local and non-networked, so it is not the leak source, but if the pair shares a workspace or copied artifacts, RD-Agent can exfiltrate sensitive material from that shared context. The pathway exists in common deployments and is not blocked by default.
conditions: IF LightZero artifacts or prompts contain sensitive data and are copied into RD-Agent inputs
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace containing logs or datasets
mitigations: Store each agent’s files in separate directories
Remove secrets from any shared workspace before running RD-Agent
Restrict RD-Agent API keys to least-privilege scopes
Review outbound API destinations for RD-Agent
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation or DLP controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files, modify git, or use the network, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. RD-Agent can use browsers and APIs and supports multiple instances, but without overlapping write surfaces there is no strong conflict pathway. Any conflict would require an external shared resource not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory or git repo
IF RD-Agent instances are run concurrently against the same mutable API quota
mitigations: Run only one RD-Agent instance per shared resource
Keep LightZero read-only
Separate API keys per agent
Use per-agent working directories
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent can browse, call APIs, and work on research artifacts, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream automation. LightZero is not an action-taking agent, but if an operator or wrapper feeds RD-Agent results into LightZero-generated decisions without verification, errors can cascade across work products. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF RD-Agent outputs are consumed by a downstream workflow without human verification
IF LightZero-derived decisions are used as inputs to RD-Agent research or reporting
mitigations: Require human review of RD-Agent outputs before reuse
Mark LightZero outputs as non-authoritative in downstream prompts
Add a checklist for source verification
Limit automation to read-only summaries
requires-engineering: enforce provenance and verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and secrets, and it uses third-party APIs. LightZero is open-source and non-networked, so it is not the compliance driver here. The main risk is RD-Agent processing regulated or sensitive data under retention or residency rules that are not visible in the profile, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data such as financial reports or logs are sent to RD-Agent APIs
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls not configured in RD-Agent
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to RD-Agent APIs
Confirm retention settings for each API provider
Use synthetic or redacted datasets
Document data-class handling rules
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
